items.note: Status vocab unified to DsStatus (info|success|warning|error). Boolean input [danger] -> [error] (also static danger="..." -> error="..."). Default value unchanged.
Same danger -> error boolean-input rename on ds-modal-card.
Same danger -> error boolean-input rename on ds-menu-item.
ds-stat variant value 'danger' -> 'error'. Other variant values unchanged (absent from map — leave them).
items.verify: No ds-stat binds variant="danger". Every stat that used to be danger renders in the error colour, and stats on other variant values are untouched.

items.note: Two changes on ds-progress[variant]: 'warn' -> 'warning'; and 'indeterminate' is no longer a variant value — it becomes the boolean [indeterminate] input, so variant="indeterminate" -> the bare indeterminate attribute (a bar can now be e.g. success-coloured AND indeterminate). ProgressVariant is now 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' — TS references to the removed 'warn'/'indeterminate' members update accordingly. 'success'/'error'/'default' unchanged (absent from map).
items.verify: No `variant` remains on the component. The chips render in their status colours, not grey: the `styles/status` partial is included and any custom status is registered through DsStatusRegistry, or the colour resolves to the neutral default and you meant that.

items.note: ModalConfirmTone value 'danger' -> 'error'. Update ModalService.confirm({ tone: 'danger' }) -> { tone: 'error' } and any TS typed with ModalConfirmTone.
items.verify: No ModalService.confirm call passes `tone: 'danger'`, and nothing is typed with the removed union member.

items.note: SplitButtonItem object property `danger` renamed to `error`. Update item literals ({ danger: true } -> { error: true }) and any TS typed with SplitButtonItem.
items.verify: No SplitButtonItem literal carries `danger`; every one uses `error`.

items.note: Public token renamed in lockstep with [danger] -> [error]. CSS property and default unchanged.

The status-vocabulary rename also renamed the class the card puts on its root: [danger] used to emit `danger`, [error] now emits `error`. The input-rename item fixes the BINDING; a consumer stylesheet that keys off the class needs this one, and nothing in the binding rename would find it. Scope strictly to selectors under ds-modal / ds-modal-card.
Same rename on ds-menu-item: the host used to carry `danger`, it now carries `error`. Consumer STYLING only.
ds-stat's variant value moved danger -> error, and the host class follows it (host binding [class.error]). Consumer STYLING only; the value-remap item covers the binding.
Same as ds-stat: variant value danger -> error with a matching host class. Consumer STYLING only.
Public token renamed in lockstep with the 'warn' -> 'warning' value. CSS property and default unchanged.
Dismissal event unified to (closed): (dismissed) -> (closed) on ds-alert.
(dismissed) -> (closed) on ds-banner.
(dismissed) -> (closed) on ds-toast.
Action event made past-tense: (rowClick) -> (rowClicked) on ds-table.
(stepClick) -> (stepClicked) on ds-stepper.
(daySelect) -> (daySelected) on ds-calendar-day.

title is now REQUIRED on ds-drawer, ds-bottom-sheet, and ds-accordion-item (it is the component's accessible name / disclosure-button label). Add a [title]/title if any instance is missing one. ds-page-header title is now OPTIONAL (plain <h1>) — no action there.
items.verify: Every ds-drawer, ds-bottom-sheet and ds-accordion-item carries a title - it is the component's accessible name, and a missing one leaves the disclosure button unlabelled.

items.note: ds-badge [variant] (BadgeVariant) renamed to [status] (typed DsStatusKey); the value is emitted as a data-status attribute, NOT a factory/status-named CSS class, and the component ships NO built-in colour for any value. Full migration is THREE coupled steps — the rename alone leaves badges uncoloured: (1) rename the input, keeping the value: variant="active" -> status="active", [variant]="expr" -> [status]="expr" (a static variant="x" left on ds-badge is a SILENT failure — Angular ignores the unknown attribute rather than erroring — so grep variant= scoped to ds-badge). (2) Wire colours via the styles/status SCSS API keyed on [data-status] (see status-lifecycle-tokens-removed for the @use/@include snippet). (3) For TS type-safety, augment DsStatusRegistry with your keys so DsStatusKey narrows from open string to your union. NOTE for consumers who coloured badges via their OWN status-named class (class="chip {{ status }}" + ds-badge.chip.completed{...}) instead of [variant]: that keeps working (the --ds-badge-* hooks are unchanged), BUT any value that previously fell through to a FACTORY colour is now uncoloured — move colour off the class onto [data-status] via styles/status. Full guide + before/after: migrations/0.5.1/badge-statuses.md. [count]/[solid]/[withDot]/[max] and the --ds-badge-* hooks are unchanged.
items.verify: No `variant` remains on the component. The chips render in their status colours, not grey: the `styles/status` partial is included and any custom status is registered through DsStatusRegistry, or the colour resolves to the neutral default and you meant that.

items.note: ds-status-dot [status] keeps its name but is retyped StatusValue -> DsStatusKey and no longer defaults to 'planning'; the value is now emitted as a data-status attribute, not a `.status-dot <value>` CSS class. Any custom CSS targeting .status-dot.active / .planning / .confirmed / .completed / .warning / .error / .secondary must switch to [data-status='...']. Define status colours via the styles/status SCSS API.
items.verify: No CSS targets `.status-dot.<value>` (the value is a data-status attribute now) and nothing types a status with StatusValue instead of DsStatusKey.
items.restore: status="planning" stated explicitly, where a dot relied on the old default

items.note: The exported types BadgeVariant, BadgeLifecycle, BadgeSemantic (badge) and StatusValue (status-dot) are no longer exported. Type badge/status-dot status with DsStatusKey (or your own registered union via DsStatusRegistry augmentation).
items.verify: None of the four removed type names is imported; badge and status-dot statuses are typed DsStatusKey or a registry-augmented union.

items.note: The factory lifecycle status theme tokens --status-planning-bg-color / -text-color, --status-confirmed-*, --status-active-*, --status-completed-* are removed. If you set them to theme lifecycle badges/dots, declare your statuses instead via the styles/status SCSS API, which writes the public --ds-badge-* / --ds-status-dot-* tokens keyed on [data-status]. Example: `@use '@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/styles/status' as status; @include status.define(('completed': (bg: var(--success), text: var(--text-on-success)), 'active': (bg: var(--info-subtitle), text: var(--info-text))));` — one entry per status value you pass to ds-badge/ds-status-dot [status]; entry shape is (bg required, text?, dot?); or use status.semantic-preset for the info/success/warning/error/neutral set. Pair with the DsStatusRegistry TS augmentation (see badge-variant-to-status-rename) so [status] is type-checked. Full guide: migrations/0.5.1/badge-statuses.md. The dimension token --status-dot-size is NOT removed.
items.verify: No stylesheet declares a --status-<lifecycle>-* token; a themed lifecycle status is declared through the styles/status Sass API instead.

items.note: Default secondary/tertiary hues changed: --secondary-h/s/l now default to the --orange palette family (warm orange) and --tertiary-h/s/l to --violet (cool violet), where they previously both defaulted to --primary channels (blue). Consumers who never set --secondary-h/s/l or --tertiary-h/s/l now render orange/violet where they saw blue — VISUAL REVIEW (usually no code change). To keep the old single-hue look, set --secondary-h/s/l and --tertiary-h/s/l back to var(--primary-h/s/l).
items.restore: --secondary-h/s/l and --tertiary-h/s/l pointed back at the --primary channels
items.verify: An app that never set those channels has looked at every secondary and tertiary surface (they are orange and violet now, not blue), or pins them back.

items.note: The fixed-value --static-white custom property is removed; replace any var(--static-white) with the literal keyword white (identical value, no visual change). --static-ink is retained.
items.verify: No stylesheet reads var(--static-white); the literal `white` stands in its place.

informational: New extensible status system: DsStatusRegistry / DsStatusKey type exports + styles/status SCSS API (define($map) / semantic-preset) — the additive half of the badge/status-dot status redesign.
Additive: DsStatus type export ('info'|'success'|'warning'|'error'); ds-progress [indeterminate] boolean input; DividerSpacing now re-exported from the public API.

Visual/behavioral only, no code change: press-feedback reworked (no button-style press on non-buttons; list/menu rows and color-picker trigger get a flat :active tint; small icon action buttons — close/dismiss/clear/remove x and the ds-tag chip close — get the button press-scale); booleanAttribute coercion on ~54 boolean inputs; ds-button tonal :active now darkens past hover.

Fixes, no action required: overlay panel --ds-* overrides now reach the portaled pane (ds-autocomplete/ds-multi-select/ds-date-picker/ds-color-picker/ds-popover/ds-time-picker); ds-autocomplete/ds-multi-select panels no longer render transparent; ds-tabs secondary variant now applies; ds-date-picker range mask no longer clips the second date + tighter value-to-icon gap; the ultra-compact density tier now scales avatar/sidenav/badge/status-dot/switch geometry.

Visual/behavioral only, no code change: ds-date-picker keeps the format mask visible while typing — the unfilled tail of the mask stays on-screen as a muted ghost (e.g. "12/DD/YYYY") and the typed value renders in the monospace font for exact glyph alignment.
